name: Biophilia Hypothesis
citation: Wilson, E.O. (1984). Biophilia. Harvard University Press.

constructs.description: Organized complexity: scaling hierarchy (~2.5:1 ratios), mid-range fractal D (1.3-1.5), local symmetries, moderate edge contrast, biomorphic forms. Unifying principle: high information content with high structural predictability.
Mid-range fractal patterns (D ≈ 1.3-1.5) produce maximal processing efficiency via V1/V2 tuning to 1/f^β power spectra (β ≈ 2.6). Most directly manipulable variable in the framework.
Evolutionary preparedness for natural environments: fractal preference, natural material warmth, savanna-type landscape preference.

schema_gaps: Non-visual biophilic modalities (olfactory, thermal) not yet templated
irreducible_residual.narrative: Biophilia specifies WHAT to build so that ART and SRT mechanisms can operate. The design specification layer — prospect + refuge, organized complexity, fractal D — is an organizing principle not derivable from any single T1 framework. Non-visual biophilia (birdsong, natural scents, water sounds) extends beyond current visual-spatial reductions. Fractal Fluency also has independent T1.5 status for non-biophilic contexts (abstract art, interior surfaces).
